text:
Tage Thompson is doing what he always does, which is score from places other people can't. He has 12 goals in 20 games, a 100.17 mph shot at the very top of NHL EDGE's tracking, and he ranks fourth among 529 skaters in our wins added by goals, a measure of how much his goals moved his team's chances of winning. The Sabres have lost a lot lately; his goals have kept coming anyway, including one in each of the losses to Tampa Bay and Chicago.

The finishing isn't a fluke: he's shooting 15.2%, right at last season's rate, and his own chances (1.40 expected goals per 60, the quality of his looks) are up a touch. The soft spot is around him. Buffalo has scored 5.0 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and its five-on-five share in his minutes is an even 50%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the league's best at getting to the slot last season (93rd percentile), and Evolving-Hockey had him facing tough competition. He's the Sabres' engine; the question is whether the team around him can start tilting the ice.
